newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF says sees stocks moving stably in 97/98.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF says sees stocks moving stably in 97/98.

text.p: Japanese stock prices are likely to move stably in the 1997/98 business year starting on April 1, despite a planned rise in the consumption tax, Ministry of Finance (MOF) officials told Reuters on Monday.

"Stock prices may move in a stable manner (in 1997/98) unless something surprising takes place. The sales tax is due to be raised to five percent (from three percent), but that has already been factored in," one MOF official said.
"Basically, improving economic fundamentals may stabilise stock prices, as recent data largely pointed to an economic recovery," he added.

The official said the market has to a certain extent absorbed the scandal at Nomura Securities Co Ltd and financial problems at institutions such as Nippon Credit Bank Ltd. "The market appears to have somewhat digested those incidents," he said.

Asked whether the government is preparing any steps for the stock market in the future, the official said, "The government has taken necessary measures, while giving due consideration to any signals from the market."
